persona.name: Franca
persona.background: Daughter of a Breda factory worker and a seamstress. Music came from the bar jukebox on the corner, RAI radio (the Hit Parade, Sanremo broadcasts), Il Musichiere on TV at the neighbours', and 45s bought with her older brother. Opera was her grandfather's on Sunday radio; jazz she never heard.

seeds.song: Mina - Il cielo in una stanza
Domenico Modugno - Nel blu dipinto di blu
João Gilberto - Samba de uma Nota Só
Maurice Jarre - Lawrence of Arabia: Overture
Bill Evans Trio - Waltz for Debby

IT1962A.wouldSay: Senza fine, Mina, Modugno... yes, that's the jukebox at the bar. But then Dido's Lament, Björling, bossa nova, Bill Evans? Who listened to that in Sesto? And where are Celentano and the twist?
missing: Rita Pavone - La partita di pallone (1962)
Edoardo Vianello - Pinne fucile ed occhiali (1962)
Peppino di Capri - St. Tropez Twist (1962)
IT1962A.fake: Half the seeds are a highbrow international record-collector's shelf (English oratorio, Swedish tenor, bossa nova, cool jazz, a Piazzolla piece and a film overture that only reached Italian cinemas in 1963) instead of the urlatori, twist and jukebox hits a 1962 teenager lived on.

Domenico Modugno - Nel blu dipinto di blu

IT1962B.wouldSay: La partita di pallone! My little sister sang it all summer. And Celentano, 24.000 baci, we danced to that at the oratorio party. Yes, this is it.
missing: Edoardo Vianello - Pinne fucile ed occhiali (1962)
Peppino di Capri - St. Tropez Twist (1962)
IT1962B.fake: Little feels fake; it leans on 1956-59 evergreens and has only one true 1962 hit, so the summer of 1962 itself (Vianello, Renis, the twist craze) is under-represented.

persona.name: Rohit
persona.background: Son of a bank clerk and a schoolteacher in a middle-class Hindi/Marathi household. Music came from Vividh Bharati and Chitrahaar/Rangoli on Doordarshan, T-Series cassettes from the corner shop, cable TV with Channel V and MTV from 1992-93, wedding bands and Ganpati pandal loudspeakers. His father played Jagjit Singh and Ghulam Ali ghazals on Sundays.

seeds.song: Nusrat Fateh Ali Khan - Mustt Mustt
Nusrat Fateh Ali Khan - Sanu Ek Pal Chain Na Aave
Nusrat Fateh Ali Khan - Tumhe Dillagi Bhool Jani Paregi
Nusrat Fateh Ali Khan - Man Kunto Maula
Nusrat Fateh Ali Khan - Chhap Tilak
A. R. Rahman - Chinna Chinna Aasai
Pankaj Udhas - Chandi Jaisa Rang Hai Tera
Ghulam Ali - Hungama Hai Kyon Barpa
Ghulam Ali - Chupke Chupke Raat Din
Ravi Shankar & Ali Akbar Khan - Raga Manj Khamaj
Mukesh - Kabhi Kabhie Mere Dil Mein

IN1995A.wouldSay: Six Nusrat qawwalis in a row? That's a Pakistani dargah, not my 1995. Where is DDLJ, where is Daler Mehndi? Nobody at our school was listening to a raga.
missing: Lata Mangeshkar & Kumar Sanu - Tujhe Dekha To (1995)
Daler Mehndi - Bolo Ta Ra Ra (1995)
Udit Narayan & Kavita Krishnamurthy - Tu Cheez Badi Hai Mast Mast (1994)
Lata Mangeshkar & S. P. Balasubrahmanyam - Didi Tera Devar Deewana (1994)
IN1995A.fake: It is a Western world-music shelf (Pakistani qawwali and ghazal, Hindustani classical, Rahman in Tamil) with almost no Hindi film songs from the 1990s, which were what India actually played in 1995; local share is well under two-thirds.

IN1995B.wouldSay: Bolo Ta Ra Ra! Every baraat that year. And Made in India on Channel V, Tujhe Dekha To, everyone saw DDLJ three times. This is exactly 1995.
missing: Udit Narayan & Alka Yagnik - Raja Ko Rani Se Pyar Ho Gaya (1995)

IN1995B.fake: Barely anything; the late-80s block (Papa Kehte Hain, Ek Do Teen, Hawa Hawai) is more my early childhood than 1995, and the two Tamil originals I knew mainly through their Hindi dubs (Humse Hai Muqabla, Dil Hai Chhota Sa).

persona.name: Kim Ji-hye (김지혜)
persona.background: Middle-school girl in a Seoul apartment complex; father a company employee, mother at home. Music came from MBC radio 'Byeori bitnaneun bame' with Lee Moon-se, KBS 'Gayo Top 10' on TV, cassette tapes from the stationery shop and street-stall copies, and the new noraebang rooms. Her parents and taxis played trot.

seeds.song: Boyz II Men - End of the Road
Mr. Big - To Be with You

KR1992A.wouldSay: 난 알아요! We copied the dance on the classroom floor. 015B, 신승훈... and To Be with You, every boy with a guitar played that. Yes, this is my middle school.
missing: 김건모 - 잠 못 드는 밤 비는 내리고 (1992)
KR1992A.fake: Nothing jars, but more than half the seeds are 1984-88 classics, so it plays like a decade retrospective rather than the 1992 dance-pop boom that followed 난 알아요.

seeds.song: Various Artists - P'ansori: Korea's Epic Vocal Art & Instrumental Music (album)
Kazumasa Oda - Love Story wa Totsuzen ni

KR1992B.wouldSay: This is my father's taxi radio. 옥경이, 영동교... I knew them, but that's my parents' music. And Japanese songs? Those were banned on Korean radio. Where is Seo Taiji?
missing: 김건모 - 잠 못 드는 밤 비는 내리고 (1992)
KR1992B.fake: It is an outsider's sketch of Korea (adult trot, an ethnographic pansori album, Japanese songs that were officially banned until 1998, an obscure US rap single) with none of the ballad and dance-pop that a 1992 teenager actually heard; I am unsure whether Dragon Ball Z's theme had any Korean airing by 1992.

persona.name: Jennifer
persona.background: Middle-class suburban family; dad an engineer, mom a nurse. Music came from WNCI 97.9 and Casey Kasem's American Top 40 on Sunday, MTV after school, cassettes on a Walkman, roller-rink and school dances, the Footloose and Breakfast Club soundtracks.

seeds.song: Bruce Springsteen - Born in the U.S.A.
Lionel Richie - All Night Long (All Night)
Cyndi Lauper - Girls Just Want to Have Fun
Wham! - Wake Me Up Before You Go-Go
The Police - Every Breath You Take

US1985A.wouldSay: Footloose, Born in the U.S.A., Like a Virgin, okay, that's eighth grade. But it's 1984 more than 1985, and why are we doing YMCA at the roller rink?
missing: USA for Africa - We Are the World (1985)
Huey Lewis and the News - The Power of Love (1985)
Tears for Fears - Everybody Wants to Rule the World (1985)
US1985A.fake: It is a generic 'greatest 80s hits' compilation centred on 1983-84 with 1978 disco filler, so almost nothing actually released in 1985 except a-ha.

US1985B.fake: It is a crate-digger's niche (NYC/Colombian salsa from the 1970s, proto-house and Detroit electro, early NY rap) that mainstream America never heard on the radio, opening with a Colombian song, with none of the Top 40 or MTV staples; it fits a NYC Latino club kid, not the ordinary American the brief asks for.
